principals.purpose: Executes the single-linearization-point Spanner Commit RPC (ADR-044 §5, spannercommit.Client.Commit) and the GCS witness create/read operations (ADR-044 §6, gcswitness.Adapter.CreateExactIfAbsent/ReadExact/Exists) that together constitute the Recovery Authority's non-signing runtime. ADR-044 §15 explicitly permits the witness writer and witness reader/verifier to share one runtime principal; this principal is that combination plus the Spanner commit path, since all three are the same non-signing execution context.
principals.credential_model: Workload Identity Federation (e.g. GKE Workload Identity) bound to the Recovery Authority runtime workload only -- no static service-account key file, ever (ADR-044 §15, ADR-045 §5).
principals.rotation_responsibility: No credential material to rotate under Workload Identity Federation. IAM binding changes for this principal are the authority/witness administrative domain's responsibility (ADR-044 §15), reviewed independently of any signing-domain (§domain=signing) change (ADR-045 §4 property 2).
principals.notes: roles/spanner.databaseUser is deliberately NOT used: independently re-verified against current official Cloud Spanner IAM documentation, that predefined role also bundles spanner.databases.updateDdl and spanner.databases.getDdl (schema mutation/read capability) alongside its data-plane permissions -- granting it would give this runtime principal DDL capability ADR-044 §15 reserves for a separate bootstrap/retention-policy administrator. This manifest therefore lists the exact custom-role permission set instead. Session/transaction orchestration above the raw Commit call (PREPARE, reads) is not yet implemented in committed code (ADR-044 §17 item 3, S5) -- the permission set above anticipates the full data-plane footprint that orchestration will need, derived from ADR-044 §5's architecture, not from a predefined role.

principals.purpose: Invokes Cloud KMS AsymmetricSign against exactly one caller-configured CryptoKeyVersion to produce COMMITTED V2 writer signatures (ADR-045 §5, §10; kmssigner.Signer.SignCommittedDigest).
principals.credential_model: Workload Identity Federation, resolved entirely within the independently administered signing project (ADR-045 §4) -- no shared organization/folder/parent-resource IAM inheritance with the authority/witness domain, and no static service-account key.
principals.rotation_responsibility: Signing-domain administrators (ADR-045 §5) own this principal's IAM binding and the underlying key lifecycle (§6, §7C). Authority/witness domain administrators have no IAM path to modify it (ADR-045 §4 property 1).
principals.notes: Cloud KMS IAM policies cannot be bound at the individual CryptoKeyVersion level -- independently re-verified against current official documentation ('You cannot set IAM permissions on a key version'). Binding is therefore necessarily at the CryptoKey level (this manifest's finest supported granularity); the restriction to exactly one active CryptoKeyVersion is enforced by kmssigner.Signer's own fixed, single-version construction-time configuration (ADR-045 §6), not by IAM. This does not weaken ADR-045 §7B's guidance, which is explicitly conditioned on 'where the provider's IAM model permits version-level granularity' -- it does not for this provider, a fact this manifest records rather than assumes.

principals.purpose: Retrieves a CryptoKeyVersion's lifecycle state and public key while it is ENABLED, to durably pin its verification material (ADR-045 §7C; keypinning.CaptureFromKMS). Invoked only as an administrative step of the governed key-rotation procedure (§7C steps a-c), never by ordinary runtime traffic.
principals.credential_model: Workload Identity Federation, signing-domain, a DISTINCT principal from recovery-signing -- deliberately never sharing an identity, so a compromise of one never yields the other's capability (cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.viewPublicKey vs. .useToSign is Cloud KMS's own documented IAM permission separation).
principals.rotation_responsibility: Signing-domain administrators; invoked only within the §7C governed rotation procedure, not standing runtime access.
principals.notes: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.list is deliberately excluded even though roles/cloudkms.viewer bundles it -- keypinning.CaptureFromKMS always names one exact CryptoKeyVersion and never enumerates a CryptoKey's versions, so list is unused capability, not merely inconvenient.

principals.purpose: Appends compromise/distrust declarations (ADR-045 §7) to the governed compromise ledger.
principals.credential_model: Not yet grounded in a concrete provider-backed implementation; when one is built (S4+ follow-up), it must use its own Workload Identity Federation principal in its own administrative domain, per ADR-045 §7 property 2: administratively independent of, and unreachable by, ordinary signing-domain administrators.
principals.rotation_responsibility: Not yet assignable -- compromiseledger.FileLedger (the current implementation) is explicitly qualification-grade, local-filesystem-backed, and documented in its own package comments as not the eventual production mechanism.
principals.notes: No live GCP API call exists anywhere in the compromiseledger package today (verified by direct source inspection) -- required_permissions is therefore empty by evidence, not by oversight (Phase 2: do not invent capabilities not required by code/ADR). forbidden_permissions forbids MUTATING an existing entry (update/delete) and every cross-domain capability, but deliberately does not forbid a future object-create-style append permission on this ledger's own eventual storage resource -- append-only durability requires creating new entries; ADR-045 §7's append-only property is about never editing/deleting a PRIOR entry, not about prohibiting writes altogether. Building that implementation and deriving its real permission set (including which storage.objects.create-shaped grant, on which distinct ledger-only resource) is future, separately-scoped work -- this manifest does not perform it prematurely.

principals.purpose: Read-only cross-check and recovery-runbook verification (ADR-044 §13; docs/runbooks/RECOVERY_AUTHORITY_PRODUCTION_RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md §5, §11): reads the Spanner authority_head row and the exact GCS witness object, never writes either.
principals.notes: No dedicated production Go entry point exists yet that performs these reads under a distinct runtime identity (the only current read paths are test/emulator-only, e.g. conformance/spanneradapter.ReadAuthorityHead). This principal's permission set is derived from the accepted S8 runbook's documented read-only procedure, not from landed runtime code, and is recorded so a future read entry point (S5+) is built against an already-reviewed least-privilege boundary rather than inheriting recovery-authority-runtime's write capability by convenience.

principals.purpose: Represented here ONLY as an explicit exclusion boundary. Schema/DDL, Spanner instance/database creation, GCS bucket creation and retention-policy locking, and Cloud KMS key/key-ring creation are NOT granted to any principal above -- they belong to a governed bootstrap/provisioning mechanism that ADR-044 §17 item 5 records as not yet existing (S6, not authorized by this task).
principals.notes: Full design of this principal (exact permission set, provisioning tool, credential model) is S6 scope and is explicitly NOT begun here, per this task's instruction not to start S5/S6/S7. Its presence in this inventory exists solely so every other principal's forbidden_permissions list can be checked against a named placeholder for 'the capabilities that belong to bootstrap, not runtime' rather than leaving that boundary implicit.
